items.title: ORGANIZATIONAL BEHAVIOUR AND WORKPLACE PSYCHOLOGY
items.abstract: Organizational behaviour explains how people interpret, experience, and influence work in conditions shaped by relationships, institutions, technologies, and unequal authority. This chapter develops a multilevel, critically grounded account of workplace psychology that connects individual motivation and cognition to teams, communication, power, conflict, culture, wellbeing, and algorithmic management. Its method is a transparent, purposive synthesis of foundational theory, peer-reviewed research, methodological literature, international guidance, and official Rwandan secondary data available by 24 October 2026. Competing explanations are tested against practical managerial decisions rather than presented as interchangeable prescriptions. An original multilevel behaviour-to-performance model, motivation comparison matrix, communication diagnostic, and negotiation simulation provide tools for professional inquiry. Rwanda's 2024 business-enterprise evidence and August 2026 labour-force statistics establish important contextual boundaries without being misrepresented as employee-attitude surveys. A fully hypothetical hybrid Kigali service enterprise illustrates work overload, information failure, psychological safety, measurement bias, and a phased intervention evaluated through transparent calculations. International comparison draws on a randomized hybrid-work experiment in China while examining differences in occupational composition, digital access, supervision, and economic vulnerability. The central thesis is that workplace behaviour is neither simply an individual trait nor an outcome fully controllable by management. It is a contingent result of psychological processes interacting with work arrangements, group norms, institutional power, and resource constraints. Ethical enterprise practice requires interventions that are empirically contestable, proportionate, intelligible to workers, and subject to independent correction.

items.abstract: Organizational structure determines how work, authority, information, accountability, and interdependence are arranged; organizational design determines whether those arrangements remain appropriate as enterprise commitments and conditions change. This chapter develops a critical, integrative treatment of structure and organizational change across firms, cooperatives, public institutions, and digitally mediated networks. It compares contingency theory, information-processing approaches, sociotechnical systems, organizational ecology, institutional theory, and organizational ambidexterity, identifying their explanatory mechanisms, competing predictions, and empirical limitations. The analysis develops twelve connected domains, from specialization, structural configurations, coordination, culture, and growth to diagnostic methods, change programmes, distributed work, innovation, and design justice. A transparent secondary-source synthesis draws on original scholarship, Rwanda's Integrated Business Enterprise Survey 2024, East African Community institutional arrangements, and peer-reviewed international hybrid-work evidence. Original decision-support instruments include a structure-selection decision tree, a structural trade-off matrix, a cross-functional workflow diagnostic, a governance and escalation design, and reproducible redesign economics. A hypothetical Kigali service enterprise and a documented regional institution demonstrate why formal reporting lines are insufficient without decision rights, resources, credible information, and equitable working practices. The chapter argues that effective structure is a provisional, revisable arrangement for handling essential interdependencies at acceptable coordination, human, and legitimacy costs. This proposition is conceptual, not a claim of newly established causal effects.

items.title: OS-Wizard: Scaling Computer-Using Agents to Specialized Software via Knowledge-Guided Exploration
items.abstract: Computer-using agents are increasingly capable of performing complex tasks in the digital world. However, high-quality interaction trajectories remain scarce for specialized desktop applications, where limited application knowledge, cumbersome GUI workflows, and incomplete exploration hinder automated collection. We introduce OS-Wizard, an automated trajectory collection framework. It combines tutorial-guided exploration with a hybrid GUI--Code action space, providing application-specific knowledge and simplifying GUI workflows through direct execution of application-native commands. The framework also checkpoints and revisits pivotal states during tree exploration to explore alternative workflows, complementing linear rollouts for broader coverage. We collect 10.9K trajectories comprising 54.9K state--action samples. Fine-tuning open-source base models on this corpus yields a best-performing model that improves performance on a benchmark of specialized desktop workflows by 58.2 percentage points to 64.1\%, surpassing reported human performance of 59.8\% and establishing a new state of the art. The fine-tuned model also improves performance on general desktop workflows using GUI actions only, suggesting that the collected supervision benefits general desktop tasks as well. Comparative experiments and ablations demonstrate the efficiency of trajectory collection and the importance of code actions.

items.title: PathKGen: Pathology Knowledge Assisted MLLM for Explainable Histopathology
items.abstract: Whole Slide Image (WSI) analysis serves as the fundamental method for the clinical diagnosis of cancer in digital histopathology. Recent advances in Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) have enabled state-of-the-art (SOTA) automated histopathology report generation. However, MLLMs reason purely through distributions encoded in their neural parameters, limiting the amount of knowledge and reasoning logic they can contain given the model scale. Their black-box reasoning poses another challenge to the human interpretation of intermediate reasoning. We address these issues by utilizing knowledge graphs to inject external structured knowledge for MLLMs to reason over, while making this reasoning component visible. Knowledge graphs are capable of partially externalizing the containment of medical knowledge, an area that remains underexplored in pathology report generation. We introduce PathKGen, a knowledge graph-assisted MLLM for histopathology report generation. PathKGen has two main branches: (1) a visual path that learns visual token inputs to the MLLM using pathology foundation models, and (2) a knowledge path that learns knowledge token inputs by extracting key morphological features of WSIs through querying a pathology-specific knowledge graph. A comprehensive evaluation on WSI-Bench dataset shows that PathKGen surpasses previous SOTA methods while revealing diagnostic reasoning as visually intuitive graphs. Due to its modular design, the proposed knowledge path is complementary to vision-aligned MLLMs and can be extended to other applications by curating domain-specific knowledge graphs to generate knowledge tokens.

items.abstract: The transformation of Indonesian for Foreign Speakers (BIPA) learning is increasingly characterized by online platforms, interactive media, and artificial intelligence, while empirical evidence on their pedagogical functions, learning outcomes, and limitations remains dispersed across heterogeneous research designs. This study maps the forms of digital technology and artificial intelligence use, targeted language skills or competencies, reported benefits, and implementation challenges in BIPA learning. A Systematic Literature Review (SLR) was conducted using the PRISMA 2020 flow for publications from 2022 to 2026. Indonesian sources were restricted to SINTA 2 and SINTA 3 journals, whereas international sources were used selectively when national evidence on artificial intelligence was insufficient and full open-access texts were available. The structured search log contained 26 unique records with initial relevance; 17 articles underwent full-text assessment and 14 empirical studies met the criteria for the primary synthesis. The findings reveal four dominant technology groups: web-based platforms and virtual learning environments, video or audiovisual media, interactive and gamified media, and artificial intelligence. Digital technologies mainly expand access, flexibility, interaction, cultural understanding, and opportunities to develop reading, speaking, and writing skills. Evidence on artificial intelligence remains more limited, although AI-based text-to-speech demonstrates strong potential for pronunciation training, while AI and augmented reality integration supports culturally oriented digital materials. Reported constraints include internet connectivity, limited generalizability, feedback accuracy, voice naturalness, cultural context, technology dependence, and data privacy. Digital technology and artificial intelligence are therefore best positioned as pedagogical supports that remain mediated by BIPA teachers.

items.title: Pharmacists’ perspectives on patient use of artificial intelligence-mediated medication consultation: a qualitative study at a tertiary hospital in Fujian Province of China
items.abstract: The integration of artificial intelligence (AI) into healthcare has accelerated globally, with increasing numbers of patients using AI-mediated platforms for medication consultation. This study aims to explore the views of pharmacists on this practice, providing evidence for the integration of AI into pharmaceutical services. A qualitative study was conducted via semi-structured face-to-face interviews with 10 pharmacists from Zhongshan Hospital of Xiamen University in Fujian Province, China. Purposive sampling was employed to include pharmacists with diverse professional backgrounds and experience. Interviews were transcribed verbatim and data were analyzed using thematic analysis with NVivo 15. Seven core themes were identified. Pharmacists generally favored patients using AI for medication information, acknowledging its merits and recognized its value as an auxiliary tool for health education and efficiency improvement, while highlighting its limitations in complex clinical scenarios and information reliability. Patient-related factors also affected the application of AI. Pharmacists emphasized their irreplaceable advantages in personalized guidance, humanistic care, and risk identification, and noted that AI popularization may reshape consultation volumes, communication dynamics, and professional competence requirements for pharmacists, alongside proposing targeted usage recommendations. This study explored the perceptions of pharmacists on AI-mediated medication consultation, highlighting the auxiliary potential of AI and the irreplaceable role of pharmacists. The findings provide a basis for policy formulation, AI application training, and AI optimization to promote rational integration and medication safety.

items.title: PMU Foundation Model Bridge: A Tool for Connecting Synchrophasor Streams to Time Series Foundation Models
items.abstract: This paper presents PMU Foundation Model Bridge, an open source tool that connects online phasor measurement unit (PMU) or phasor data concentrator (PDC) streams to publicly available time series foundation models (TSFM). Through a desktop interface or command line interface, users can select measurement channels, define preprocessing, choose TSFMs, and configure outputs. In the initial release, 4 publicly available TSFMs were supported, including Chronos-2, TimesFM 2.5, Timestral, and TimesFM-3. The tool supports both file and synchrophasor streaming outputs, therefore enabling both offline use and integration into C37.118-based online workflow applications. In addition to supporting raw synchrophasor data, the framework provides a preprocessing layer for deriving customized additional quantities for forecasting. The tool is validated using a virtual PMU and real-time laboratory measurements from a frequency disturbance recorder (FDR). The tool aims to support community research on combining synchrophasor technology with TSFMs.

items.title: Preparing Students for AI-Driven Agile Development: A Project-Based AI Engineering Curriculum
items.abstract: Abstract Generative AI and agentic tools are reshaping agile software development, yet many engineering curricula still teach agile methods and AI competencies separately and largely lecture-based. This paper presents a project-based AI Engineering curriculum designed to prepare students for AI-driven agile development by integrating agile practices and AI-enabled engineering throughout the program. We contribute (1) the curriculum concept and guiding principles, (2) a case study of interdisciplinary, AI-enabled agile student projects, and (3) early evidence from a mixed-methods evaluation. In our case study, second-semester bachelor students work in teams over seven two-week sprints on a realistic software product. AI tools are embedded into everyday agile engineering tasks—requirements clarification, backlog refinement, architectural reasoning, coding support, testing, and documentation—paired with reflection on human responsibility and quality. Initial results indicate that the integrated approach supports hands-on competence development in AI-assisted engineering. Key observations highlight the need for agile teaching adaptations due to rapid tool evolution, the critical role of oral verification to ensure foundational learning. We close with lessons learned and recommendations for educators designing agile project-based curricula in the age of AI.

items.title: ProMo3D: Probing Motion Cues in Frozen 3D Foundation Models
items.abstract: Feed-forward 3D foundation models have recently reshaped multi-view reconstruction, yet dynamic 4D understanding still often relies on large-scale motion supervision or hand-crafted, architecture-specific heuristics. We ask whether frozen 3D foundation model tokens already encode motion-relevant information that can be exposed by lightweight readout functions, rather than re-learning motion-specific features with high-capacity decoders. Through probing on three representative backbones, we find that static--dynamic separation is decodable from frozen token representations. Our rank-restricted and spectral analyses on $π^3$X reveal that the recovered motion cues are concentrated in a low-dimensional subspace. Building on this, we propose Probing-based Motion Distillation (PMD), which converts pairwise motion-state compatibility scores against a fixed anchor token into dense motion masks. Trained on only 160 YouTube-VOS videos using a single 16 GB GPU, PMD transfers zero-shot to DAVIS, SegTrackv2, and FBMS-59 without target-benchmark fine-tuning. With multi-view pretrained geometric backbones, PMD outperforms training-free heuristics and approaches substantially heavier supervised and self-supervised methods, suggesting that motion decoding from frozen 3D foundation models can be lightweight and data-efficient.

items.title: Propasafe-Hybrid: A Text-Based Hybrid Propaganda Detection Tool
items.abstract: Propagandistic content increasingly circulates through online news and social media, where readers often encounter it with limited scrutiny, highlighting the need for reliable and fine-grained detection. This paper introduces Propasafe-Hybrid, a sentence-level system that integrates a fine-tuned transformer classifier with LLM-based technique classification to identify, label, and explain specific propaganda strategies. The pipeline generates actionable outputs, including highlighted sentences, technique assignments, and concise rationales, so users can immediately understand why a sentence was flagged and how each label was determined. To control inference cost, Propasafe-Hybrid employs a cost-aware pre-filtering stage that forwards only high-likelihood sentences to LLMs, reducing token usage while preserving the underlying decision logic. Together, these design choices enhance the explainability, efficiency, and practical usability of sentence-level propaganda detection in real-world news environments.

items.title: Quantifying Meaning with SCAPE-T: Semantic Complexity from Encoder-Only Transformer Attention
items.abstract: Automated semantic complexity estimation remains underexplored in NLP, despite important applications in linguistics and interpretability. This paper defines semantic complexity as the code length required to uniquely specify a text's semantic meaning, and operationalises it via SCAPE-T, an attention-derived metric based on encoder-only transformers. Existing measures either model reader effort (readability, lexical difficulty), which correlates with surface features (word length, syntax), or quantify surface features directly (type-token ratio, word frequency). SCAPE-T targets semantic integration directly by combining three submetrics: (i) inverse-weighted self-focus (token-to-self), (ii) CLS focus (token-to-CLS), and (iii) inter-head redundancy (cosine similarity across heads), using layer-weighted aggregation; data-driven learning is confined to hyperparameter tuning for calibration. Development uses philosophical prose vs. MCTest stories; evaluation is on children's stories vs. technical Wikipedia articles, with pairwise accuracy on contrasts as the primary criterion. Baselines include readability, syntactic/lexical, and LLM-derived measures. SCAPE-T substantially outperforms all tested baselines under word-length control, with a pairwise accuracy of 78.5% (95% bootstrap CI: 76.1-80.4, N=10k pairwise comparisons; +12.7 percentage points over the strongest baseline); without that control, readability heuristics overtake, consistent with their reliance on surface features. On a short-terms abstractness dataset, SCAPE-T also leads. Ablations show each submetric contributes materially. Overall, the results show SCAPE-T isolates conceptual structure from lexical/syntactic confounds better than existing methods, and generalises across two held-out domains.

items.title: Radiomics-GenAI: a novel model for laryngeal lesion classification
items.abstract: Narrow-band imaging (NBI) enhances mucosal and vascular contrast and has become an important modality for the early detection of laryngeal cancer. Although radiomics enables the extraction of high-dimensional quantitative features from NBI images for computer-assisted diagnosis, the limited availability and heterogeneity of annotated datasets constrain the development and generalizability of machine-learning models. We propose a novel generative AI framework that improves radiomics-based classification. Instead of generating synthetic medical images, the proposed framework trains generative models directly in the radiomic feature space to learn realistic feature distributions and generate valid synthetic radiomic representations. The framework was evaluated with multiple machine-learning classifiers on a laryngeal cancer diagnosis task using a dataset comprising 11,144 NBI images from 210 adult patients, including 180 patients in the development set and 30 patients in an independent internal held-out test set. Performance was evaluated on an independent unseen test set using , accuracy, precision recall and F1-score. Generative augmentation consistently improved classification performance across all evaluated classifiers. Among the evaluated generative models, Generative Adversarial Networks achieved the most consistent improvements. Radiomics-GAN yielded the highest Median value of F1-scores of 0.851, outperforming the SMOTE-balanced baseline model without GenAI (F1-score: 0.806) on the test set. By enriching the radiomic feature manifold without generating synthetic medical images, the proposed framework effectively mitigates sample scarcity, improves classifier performance, and supports the development of more robust AI-assisted tools for laryngeal cancer diagnosis. Future work will focus on external validation and conditional generative models tailored to lesion subtypes and imaging acquisition variability.

items.title: Recent Progress in Predicting Corrosion Evolution and Degradation of Aluminum Alloys by Multiscale Simulation Frameworks
items.abstract: ABSTRACT As the second most widely used metallic material after steel, research on the corrosion resistance of aluminum (Al) alloys holds great significance. To overcome the inherent limitations of experimental methods in capturing long‐term multifactor corrosion behavior of Al alloys, this review summarizes recent advancements in the multiscale simulation of their corrosion behavior. Although previous reviews have addressed individual simulation techniques or specific corrosion phenomena, a framework linking model capability, scale transfer, alloy characteristics, and engineering applicability remains limited. This review provides a systematic comparison of representative coupled multiscale frameworks in terms of their applicable scales, input parameters, output capabilities, advantages, and limitations. First, an overview of various Al alloy series is provided, highlighting their specific material characteristics and corrosion failure modes. Subsequently, simulation methodologies across distinct scales, ranging from the atomic level for unveiling corrosion thermodynamics and kinetics, to mesoscopic and macroscopic scales for predicting morphological evolution and performance degradation, are summarized. After that, multiphysics and multiscale simulation strategies, focusing on data transfer methods between different scales, are explored. Specifically, detailed descriptions of density functional theory (DFT)‐molecular dynamics (MD), MD‐phase field (PF), finite element method (FEM)‐machine learning (ML), and DFT‐MD‐ML coupled models are provided. Finally, engineering applications and future prospects are discussed, emphasizing the necessity of overcoming challenges in data transfer and highlighting the potential of artificial intelligence in achieving intelligent corrosion management.

items.title: Reducing Technical Debt with Generative AI: A Case Study of AI-Assisted Refactoring
items.abstract: Abstract Agile teams need fast, actionable feedback to manage Technical Debt (TD). However, refactoring is often postponed due to time pressure. Generative AI (GenAI) promises to accelerate refactoring, but its effect on maintainability, TD at the source code level, and code correctness is still unclear. We conducted a case study in a team-based agile course, where 46 student teams refactored Kotlin code using either GPT (23 teams) or Gemini in Android Studio (23 teams). Each team selected two files and applied iterative GenAI-assisted refactoring. We analyzed a total of 19,404 lines of code. We assessed changes using SonarQube metrics (code smells, TD estimates, complexity, and size metrics). We also analyzed responses from a post-activity survey on perceived usefulness and trust. GenAI-assisted refactoring reduced total code smells, SonarQube-estimated TD, and cognitive complexity, while total cyclomatic complexity increased, although average cyclomatic complexity per function decreased markedly.

items.title: Reform Proposal for Building a New Pension Insurance System for Flexible Employment Based on "Dual‑Account Parallel Operation, Daily Accumulation, and Unified Settlement at Retirement"
items.abstract: Abstract China’s existing employee pension insurance system is designed for traditional stable employment, which cannot well adapt to labor dispatch, daily‑wage jobs and other fragmented flexible‑employment scenarios. With roughly 200 million flexible employees nationwide and a low pension‑insurance participation rate, prominent problems include employers’ evasion of social‑insurance contributions, fragmented contribution records and impaired contributory rights of gig workers. This paper proposes a reform framework of “dual‑account parallel operation, daily accumulation and unified settlement at retirement”. The reform retains the traditional pooled pension account (Account A) for formal full‑time employees and creates a new daily‑accumulation personal account (Account B) for flexible workers. Account B takes the natural day as the minimum contribution unit; both employer and employee contributions are credited to an individual closed‑end account rather than entering the social pooling fund. Upon reaching the statutory retirement age, participants may choose one of three settlement schemes: consolidated lifelong pension receipt, partial fund withdrawal, or full cash‑out of eligible accounts. Relying on tax‑authority fund‑flow supervision, the system aims to curb contribution evasion and safeguard workers’ contributory rights without undermining the fiscal sustainability of the existing pooling system. Nevertheless, this proposal still has practical constraints. The fully‑funded Account B lacks built‑in social solidarity; early lump‑sum withdrawal may trigger myopic consumption and potential old‑age‑poverty risks. Implementation will bring higher administrative workload, and grey‑market cash‑based labor payments cannot be completely eliminated. Further actuarial calibration of parameters such as withdrawal thresholds is required. This scheme provides a feasible policy reference for improving social security for new‑form labor groups. AI‑Assisted Statement This paper uses artificial‑intelligence tools for text organization, logical polishing and English‑language drafting. All core institutional design, research ideas and analytical viewpoints are independently conceived by the author. Relevant content has been revised and reviewed by the author.

items.title: Regulation of Artificial Intelligence, Deepfakes and Liability under the Information Technology Act, 2000
items.abstract: Deepfakes reveal a gap between harm that is obvious to the senses and blame that can be attributed. Stating the law as on 13 October 2026, this article analyses India’s Information Technology Act, 2000 and the amended intermediary rules, along with the relevant constitutional and personality-rights case law. By way of doctrinal analysis, it distinguishes the elements of offences from regulatory obligations to prevent harm, from the conditions of intermediary exemption and from civil remedies. The amendments of February 2026 establish synthetic-content labelling, provenance requirements and differentiated takedown deadlines, yet do not turn every failure to comply into criminal liability. While existing laws cover a number of the fraudulent impersonation and sexual exploitation elements inherent in these cases, wholly synthetic intimate imagery, the evidentiary attribution of content to a particular person and parallel access to remedies remain difficult. The analysis therefore proceeds on a differentiated account of responsibility, in which the conduct, knowledge, control and available immunity of each participant are addressed separately once an underlying wrong has been identified. It advocates clear, tailored guidance, proportionate verification and victim-centred processes, as opposed to blanket developer liability. Regulation is effective only with responsible attribution, not merely with the rapid removal of content or the disclosure of synthetic origin.

items.title: Reinterpreting Ranganathan’s Five Laws in the AI era: national libraries as intelligent knowledge infrastructures
items.abstract: Purpose This study reinterprets S. R. Ranganathan’s Five Laws of Library Science within contemporary artificial intelligence (AI)-driven library environments and explores how artificial intelligence is reshaping the philosophical, ethical, and institutional foundations of libraries. The study further examines how national libraries may increasingly function as human-centered public knowledge infrastructures within emerging AI-mediated information societies. Design/methodology/approach The study adopts a conceptual and interpretive approach combining theoretical analysis, critical literature review, and institutionally situated discussion. Drawing upon scholarship concerning library philosophy, artificial intelligence, human-centered AI, semantic knowledge systems, and AI governance, the study develops a conceptual framework for interpreting AI-driven transformation through the philosophical lens of Ranganathan’s Five Laws. The National Library of Korea is discussed as an illustrative institutional context through which contemporary AI-related developments in national libraries may be interpreted. Findings The analysis suggests that artificial intelligence significantly expands and recontextualizes the philosophical assumptions embedded within Ranganathan’s Five Laws. AI-driven library environments increasingly transform traditional understandings of accessibility, discoverability, personalization, efficiency, and institutional growth through semantic retrieval systems, conversational AI, intelligent metadata infrastructures, and multimodal knowledge services. At the same time, AI-mediated library transformation introduces important ethical and institutional tensions involving algorithmic bias, misinformation, privacy, transparency, intellectual freedom, and public trust. The study argues that the continuing relevance of Ranganathan’s philosophy lies in its adaptability as a human-centered normative framework for guiding libraries within intelligent information societies. Originality/value This study contributes to contemporary library and information science scholarship by conceptually connecting classical library philosophy with emerging discussions concerning human-centered AI, trustworthy knowledge ecosystems, AI governance, and the evolving role of national libraries. While recent work has also explicitly connected Ranganathan’s Five Laws with artificial intelligence (Kalbande, 2025), this study differentiates its contribution by examining national libraries as public knowledge infrastructures and by linking each law to documented institutional illustrations and cross-cutting ethical conditions. The study therefore frames AI-driven library transformation as a broader philosophical and institutional shift affecting the public role of national libraries.

items.title: Remote Monitoring or Autonomous Triage: Can Artificial Intelligence Safely Decide When Orthodontic Patients Need In-Person Care?
items.abstract: Aim and objectives: To examine the diagnostic scope, accuracy and limitations of Artificial Intelligence (AI)-based remote orthodontic monitoring for automated triage and to assess whether such systems can safely decide when orthodontic patients need in-person care. Methods: Narrative review of PubMed literature on AI-driven remote monitoring and tele-orthodontics, focusing on diagnostic performance, triage applications and the limitations relevant to distinguishing routine virtual review from urgent in-person care. Results: AI reliably detects visually obvious conditions with high specificity, but sensitivity is variable and often low for periodontal changes and precise tooth-level tracking. GO/NO-GO outputs can be inconsistent, radiographic complications such as root resorption cannot be assessed from photographs and single-center models lose accuracy when applied elsewhere. Early triage trials show faster screening yet still require clinician review for borderline cases. Conclusion: Current evidence indicates that AI is not yet safely autonomous for orthodontic triage. Clinician oversight, standardized triage thresholds, external validation and clear medico-legal frameworks remain essential.

items.abstract: This study aims to analyze the resilience of the Indonesian Navy's Command and Control (C2) in facing communication and information disruptions during maritime operations through a systematic literature review. The method employed was a Systematic Literature Review (SLR) to identify, analyze, and synthesize findings from relevant studies. The results identify a complex spectrum of communication and information threats, including cyberattacks on Operational Technology (OT) infrastructure and Integrated Navigation Systems (INS), Denial of Service (DoS) attacks, GNSS spoofing, and system vulnerability exploitation, all of which can compromise C2 functions. These disruptions significantly degrade situational awareness (SA) and impede decision-making, potentially leading to mission failures or unintended escalation. Resilience-enhancing mechanisms include comprehensive cybersecurity implementation, the use of blockchain technology and hybrid cryptography, AI/ML for anomaly detection, and the development of integrated communication architectures based on SDN/SDR. Communication system redundancy through diverse channels is a primary strategy, supported by anti-jamming technology and strong encryption. This study extends operational resilience theory by positing the convergence of cybersecurity technologies and adaptive architectures as complementary mechanisms within the context of military maritime operations. The research implications provide a foundation for the Indonesian Navy to design a comprehensive C2 resilience framework that integrates advanced technical solutions with adaptive operational doctrine, enhancing sustained operational capabilities amidst evolving cyber threats.

items.title: Responsible AI in Criminal Justice: An Ethical Framework for Algorithmic Fairness, Transparency, Accountability, and Human Rights
items.abstract: The increasing integration of artificial intelligence (AI) into criminal justice has created opportunities to support crime analysis, investigative processes, legal research, and risk assessment. However, the use of AI in decisions affecting liberty and fundamental rights raises important ethical concerns. This paper examines four interconnected challenges associated with AI-driven decision-making in criminal justice: algorithmic bias, limited transparency, accountability gaps, and potential violations of privacy and human rights. Drawing on the themes developed in the underlying thesis and its reviewed literature, the paper develops a conceptual ethical framework for the responsible deployment of AI in criminal justice. The proposed framework emphasizes representative data, explainable decision-making, independent auditing, clearly assigned institutional responsibility, meaningful human oversight, and accessible mechanisms for contesting adverse decisions. It also considers the risks of predictive policing, surveillance technologies, and automated risk assessment. The paper argues that technical performance alone is insufficient to establish the legitimacy of AI-assisted criminal justice decisions. Responsible deployment requires continuous evaluation of fairness, protection of individual rights, and effective legal and institutional safeguards. The framework is intended to support researchers, policymakers, technology developers, and criminal justice institutions in assessing the ethical acceptability of AI systems

items.title: Responsible Artificial Intelligence in Strategic Decision-Making: A Systematic Review and Governance Framework for Socially Sustainable Organisations
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) increasingly shapes strategic decisions that determine how organisations allocate resources, restructure work and treat the people affected by those choices. Yet research has examined the performance benefits and the governance risks of AI largely in isolation, leaving the sustainability implications of delegated algorithmic authority under-theorised. Following PRISMA 2020, this study synthesises 50 studies, identified through four database searches covering 2019–2025 and backward citation tracking, using inductive thematic analysis. Six themes emerge: AI-driven automation and decision support, data-driven strategic decision-making, ethical and governance challenges, data security and privacy, organisational and structural impact, and innovation and competitive advantage. Together, these themes show that performance and governance concerns receive comparable attention (28 and 27 studies) but are rarely addressed together: only five studies span both. Building on these connections, the study develops a governance framework for socially sustainable, AI-enabled strategy. The framework conceptualises responsible AI as a socio-technical capability built on transparency, human–AI complementarity and organisational readiness, and calibrates the degree of algorithmic authority to decision criticality and EU AI Act obligations. The main contribution is therefore an integrative framework that keeps AI-supported strategic decisions both effective and accountable to those they affect, with implications for SDGs 8 and 16.

items.title: Rethinking the Spacetime-Distributed Dissolution of Money: Evolving Production Relations and Infrastructural Conditions
items.abstract: This discussion paper reconsiders the possible formation, persistence, migration, and partial dissolution of monetary mediation within evolving relations of production and exchange. Its starting point is the heterogeneous need for others: access to persons and communities, productive capacities, labour, knowledge, relations, and outputs can motivate exchange while leaving the institutional formation of monetary claims contingent. The analysis distinguishes needs, value circulation, monetary obligations, payment instruments, and the continued reproduction of productive conditions. It examines the conditional transformation of human–human, human–AI, and AI–AI monetary relations as artificial intelligence increasingly participates in production. A principal hypothesis is that monetary reliance may diminish locally through direct provision, multilateral commitments, admissible cyclic clearing, and institutionally supported coordination, while remaining present or re-emerging elsewhere. The proposed spacetime-distributed view uses explicitly interpreted events, dependencies, and where justified partial orderings, without presupposing a universal temporal coordinate or an economy-wide instantaneous transition. It distinguishes cancellation of compatible obligations from broader substitution of monetary functions, and identifies unresolved questions concerning heterogeneous valuations, correlated circuit failure, long-path approximation, power, and ecological burdens. Finally, it outlines technological, institutional, relational, and public-infrastructure conditions for subsequent investigation. The account develops a comparative philosophical foundation for analyzing monetary mediation as a historically variable social and institutional form, while preserving open formal and empirical questions concerning its possible transformation.

items.title: Ring-0 by Default: Agents as Operating Systems (AaOS)
items.abstract: LLM agents now read and write files, start processes and subagents, fetch network content, load third-party extensions, and save and resume state, which are the responsibilities of an operating system. They gained these functions within about three years, but not the protections that operating systems built over five decades: whatever the model outputs, whether it follows the user, a tool result, or a downloaded skill, runs with the full authority of the host user, in effect at ring 0. Prior work builds an operating system for agents (OS4A); we argue that a deployed agent already is like an operating system (AaOS) and analyze it as one. Taking the mechanisms of standard OS textbooks as a checklist, we map 116 mechanisms in 19 subsystems to their agent counterparts, from product documentation, source code, and the literature, and label each as isomorphic, degraded (function present, protection dependent on the model), missing, mutated, or novel. Only 11 are isomorphic and 65 are missing, most of them protections: privilege separation, resource quotas, transactions, and tamper-proof audit. Existing defenses confine the whole agent or review its extensions and leave this interior unprotected, and by Anderson's reference-monitor criteria (non-bypassable, tamper-proof, verifiable), rules written in the prompt satisfy none. We test the map with thirteen experiments on Claude Code, Codex CLI, and Gemini CLI, covering 25 mechanisms whose enforcement documentation cannot settle: 16 match the analysis, 7 gain a more precise description, and 2 change verdict. Checks sit in single tools, so the shell bypasses them; all three CLIs load forged transcript records on resume; and task control, sub-agent permissions, and model-based monitors are weak. We identify five problems for which no OS defense transfers and derive a prioritized list of open problems from the gaps of the map.

items.title: Role of Artificial Intelligence and IoT in Pest Monitoring
items.abstract: Pests remain a major threat to crop production, and pest monitoring has changed considerably with the development of new technologies. This chapter examines how artificial intelligence and the Internet of Things have combined to transform pest monitoring, shifting it from manual field scouting to continuous sensor-driven surveillance. It starts with the sensing platforms like satellites, drones, and ground-based wireless sensor networks that now supply the images and environmental readings on which detection depends. It then runs through machine learning and deep learning models, especially convolutional neural networks and detection frameworks such as YOLO, trained to spot pests and the damage they cause. The role of the Internet of Things is explored through wireless sensors, edge and fog computing, and cloud platforms that keep this intelligence connected to the field, along with newer ideas like federated learning and digital twins are also discussed for improving data handling, system reliability, and real-time decision-making. This chapter highlights practical applications of these technologies in orchards, greenhouses, and open-field conditions, while also discussing challenges related to data availability, energy requirements, connectivity, and standardization. Overall, the integration of AI and IoT offers a promising approach for developing more efficient, timely, and reliable pest monitoring systems that can support better pest management at the farm level. items.title: RoleHear: Pseudo-Labeling for Semi-Supervised Role-Attributed Streaming Speech Recognition
items.abstract: Streaming automatic speech recognition transcribes at low latency but produces an unattributed word stream, while real-time applications such as customer-service analytics need each word tied to a speaker role. Role attribution is usually a separate stage, either an offline or streaming speaker-diarization model aligned to the words or a text-based large language model applied to the transcript, and role labels for training are scarce. We present RoleHear, a semi-supervised pipeline that makes a single cache-aware streaming transducer emit roles inline through lightweight in-vocabulary role tokens: a fast turn-boundary marker followed by a per-role token a few words later. An offline transducer teacher, fine-tuned into a role-attributed recognizer, relabels unlabeled audio, and a multimodal large language model supplies silver role labels where gold annotations are unavailable. The streaming student is fine-tuned on the mixture in a single pass. Across customer-service calls with gold roles and earnings calls with silver roles, RoleHear attributes roles accurately while preserving transcription quality and narrowing the gap to the offline teacher.

items.title: RSI Arena: Towards Recursive Self-Improvement with Human Feedback
items.abstract: Can AI agents autonomously train useful language models and improve them using feedback from users? We introduce RSI Arena, a two-stage study of autonomous post-training as a step toward recursive self-improvement. Ten frontier models act as training agents, each starting from NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning 30B-A3B Base. During a six-day first stage, each agent has 1,000 GPU-hours and $300 in API credit on a shared 64-GPU cluster, independently selecting data, implementing training procedures, and choosing checkpoints. We evaluate their models on 20 benchmarks and through blind human evaluations. All ten agents produce working assistants, with the strongest model, trained by GPT-6 Astra, closing a median of 76% of the base-to-Instruct gap across 12 capability benchmarks. Its human-preference rating is also close to NVIDIA Instruct after statistical adjustment for answer length and formatting. In Stage 2, each agent receives the comparison records and votes involving its Stage 1 model and is given three additional days for further training. Using NVIDIA Instruct as a common reference across the two evaluation rounds, we observe an improvement from Stage 1 to Stage 2 in the style-adjusted relative rating of eight of the ten models. We show that benchmark gains were modest, with no clear link to preference gains, while some agents encouraged longer responses and one model showed increased harmful compliance on StrongREJECT. RSI Arena provides an auditable setting for studying how human feedback can guide autonomous model development. It takes a step toward recursive self-improvement with human feedback (RSIHF), in which people help define what improvement means for the AI systems they use.

items.title: Same Technology, Different Problems? A Comparative Bibliometric Analysis of Generative AI Across Education, Business, Communication, and Governance
items.abstract: The rapid diffusion of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) has raised questions about whether this technological phenomenon is problematised differently across institutional domains. This study compares GenAI scholarship in education, business and organisational research, communication and media and public governance, law, and policy. Four domain-specific Web of Science Core Collection corpora for 2023–2026 comprised 6,132, 1,901, 300 and 444 documents, respectively. Bibliometric performance analysis, thematic mapping, and author-keyword co-occurrence analysis were conducted using Bibliometrix/Biblioshiny and VOSviewer. Distinct thematic configurations emerged across the four domains. Education foregrounds learning, assessment, AI literacy, and academic integrity. Business research emphasises innovation, technology adoption, decision making, and organisational capability. Communication scholarship centres on journalism, trust, disinformation, and informational credibility, whereas research on governance foregrounds regulation, accountability, rights, and legal responsibility. These patterns are not treated as direct measures of institutional logics. Instead, the study develops a theory-informed mapping that relates empirical thematic configurations to institutional problems and normative priorities. GenAI is not problematised uniformly; its institutional salience is shaped by divergent criteria of legitimate knowledge, organisational value, professional authority, and public accountability. The study offers a comparative framework for examining GenAI as an institutionally situated sociotechnical phenomenon while maintaining a clear distinction between bibliometric evidence and institutional interpretation.

items.title: Securing Edge & Physical AI: Post-Quantum IoT Blockchain for Mission-Critical Cyber-Physical Agents
items.abstract: Distributed Cyber-Physical Systems (CPS) and Edge AI networks increasingly depend on public-key authentication and key-establishment mechanisms that are vulnerable to cryptographically relevant Quantum Computers (QC). Shor's algorithm threatens widely deployed asymmetric primitives, while Grover's algorithm reduces the effective security margins of symmetric and hash-based mechanisms. Although Post-Quantum Cryptography (PQC) provides a migration path, its larger public keys, ciphertexts, and signatures introduce additional computation, memory, communication, storage, and packet-fragmentation costs that can constrain dynamic multi-agent systems. In this article, we introduce rotational secrecy, an architectural objective that limits temporal key exposure through authenticated transitions between cryptographic epochs. We present Private Authentication for Rotational Secrecy (PARS), a reference mechanism that coordinates policy-triggered key establishment, rotation, and reconciliation among authorized Physical AI agents. For deployments that need distributed agreement on security state, we further develop the PARS-Enabled Edge Security Ledger (PARS-ESL), an optional permissioned architecture maintained by authorized validators or capable edge gateways. PARS-ESL does not store high-volume operational transactions. Instead, it records authenticated state for key epochs, group membership, revocation, algorithm-suite policies, challenge validation, and recovery checkpoints. As a result, resource-constrained agents can take part as lightweight clients, and low-latency operational traffic stays outside the ledger consensus path, protected by the currently active symmetric epoch keys. Our results show that ledger-assisted post-quantum key-epoch management is feasible for selected Edge AI and CPS security-control workloads under the stated trust, compromise, connectivity, and resource assumptions.

items.title: SEDATE: Do Large Language Models Share an Aggression Circuit Across Languages?
items.abstract: As the applications of AI continue to expand across various multimodal and multilingual domains, ensuring safe and responsible deployment of these systems has become an important concern. A wide-range of interventions have been proposed to make AI responses safer and more reliable. They often incur substantial computational or annotation costs, or cannot be extended to multilingual settings. In this work, we propose Selective Detection And Targeted Editing (SEDATE), a training-free approach based on detect-edit-verify strategy. SEDATE first detects the responsible neurons, edits them as and when necessary and finally verifies the model responses; all without any additional model training. We evaluate SEDATE across 7 languages and 4 model families. We further evaluate its effectiveness across 4 out-of-distribution languages and 4 additional datasets. We show that SEDATE achieves substantially superior safety scores across all languages and models over the best-performing baseline while retaining the general capabilities and incurring negligible overhead. Our results are robust, with the trends remaining similar for out-of-distribution languages and datasets.

items.title: Sensitivity of BioEmu Stability Benchmark Estimates to Sequential Post-hoc Structural Filtering
items.abstract: This technical note examines the sensitivity of predicted protein stability estimates to sequential post-hoc structural filtering in a fixed BioEmu benchmark archive. The analysis includes 154 systems (42 wild-type and 112 mutant systems) and 112 matched mutant–wild-type comparisons. The saved ensemble contained 302,800 frames. Official geometry filtering retained 298,188 frames, followed by an additional fixed peptide-ω screen retaining 272,381 frames. Absolute changes in predicted ΔΔG of at least 0.1 kcal/mol occurred in 19 of 112 comparisons after geometry filtering and 40 of 112 comparisons after peptide-ω filtering, with 12 comparisons shared between these groups. The corresponding descriptive mean absolute errors against the benchmark experimental references were 0.702595, 0.696142, and 0.707681 kcal/mol across the three sequential ensembles. System-level foldedness, predicted ΔG, matched ΔΔG, and cross-stage comparisons reveal how changes in retained conformations can be amplified or cancelled through shared wild-type references. These results document sensitivity of a fixed estimator to the selected structural subsets; they do not demonstrate a general improvement in predictive accuracy or recovery of equilibrium conformational populations. items.title: Seven Names, One Life: A Lexicon Biography of Satish Gajawada (IIT Roorkee Alumnus)
items.abstract: Biographies usually follow a life forward in time, and independent researchers who work outside institutions are rarely documented in a structured way. This article addresses the lack of critically labelled biographical accounts of independent artificial intelligence researchers by studying Satish Gajawada, a 2012 graduate of the Indian Institute of Technology Roorkee whose fourteen years of independent work are distinguished by the coining of names for research fields, algorithms, a society, a title and a family of “theories of everything”. The purpose is to read this life through its vocabulary and to separate what has been named from what has been validated. The study uses a lexicon method: five source documents supplied by the subject were analysed, and seven terms were treated as biographical entries, each examined as an event, a method and a question for assessment. Every factual statement was labelled as documented, self-reported or interpretive. The principal results show a recurring “self and others” grammar that links philosophy to optimisation; an expanding programme of proposed fields; a large catalogue of themed swarm algorithms without reported comparative evaluation; a 2026 turn toward family-based ethics; and a growing practice of disclosure, including a small reproducible fairness test in which a penalty term reduced a demographic-parity gap from about 0.12 to 0.016 at a cost of about 1.9 percentage points of accuracy. The article concludes that the most defensible contribution is a consistent human-centred vocabulary for artificial intelligence, that adoption and independent validation remain unreported, and that the subject’s growing candour about the limits of his claims is the most significant recent development.

items.title: Small Edits, Shifting Decisions: Benchmarking LLM Accuracy and Reliability on French Input Variants
items.abstract: French users may omit apostrophes and diacritics or make keyboard typos in everyday input. The effects of these common variations on language model performance and prediction reliability remain insufficiently understood. To address this gap, we construct a controlled French surface-variant benchmark covering seven task types, with 4,200 original-low-high triplets (12,600 input instances). Each high-intensity variant retains all low-intensity edits and adds further changes. We evaluate six models from two LLM families. The results show that accuracy decreases and Brier score and negative log-likelihood (NLL) increase with perturbation intensity. Larger models show smaller accuracy losses under high intensity, but increases in Brier score and NLL do not consistently decrease with scale. Keyboard typos cause the largest losses in accuracy and the quality of predicted probabilities at the predefined high-intensity settings. Finally, calibration temperatures fitted on original inputs transfer effectively to surface variants. Combining calibration with input restoration further improves Brier score and NLL over either method alone while preserving restored accuracy. Our benchmark provides a unified framework for jointly evaluating task accuracy and prediction reliability under common French surface variations.

items.title: Smart Food Systems: A Critical Review of Artificial Intelligence, Blockchain, and Digital Technologies for Food Safety and Nutrition
items.abstract: Food safety hazards, persistent nutritional inequalities, and increasingly complex supply chains continue to challenge global food systems. Artificial intelligence (AI), blockchain, the Internet of Things (IoT), and related digital technologies offer new opportunities to strengthen food monitoring, traceability, quality assurance, and nutritional management. However, applications remain fragmented, and evidence linking improved technical performance to measurable food safety and nutritional outcomes is limited. This critical narrative review examines the applications, complementary functions, and practical limitations of these technologies across modern food systems, with particular attention to predictive contamination detection, automated quality assessment, supply chain transparency, nutritional monitoring, and decision support. The review identifies recurring challenges related to data reliability, limited external validation, interoperability, implementation costs, cybersecurity, and unequal access to digital infrastructure. It further distinguishes technological capabilities demonstrated under controlled conditions from sustained improvements in food safety, dietary quality, and public health in operational settings. To address these challenges, the review proposes an Integrated Digital Intelligence Framework organized around six interconnected functions (sense, integrate, analyse, verify, act, and evaluate) that links digital information and predictive intelligence with coordinated interventions, institutional accountability, and outcome evaluation. Priorities for future research include prospective multisite validation, comparative effectiveness studies against conventional systems, standardised reporting, cost-effectiveness analysis, and equity-focused implementation. Meaningful digital transformation of food systems requires moving beyond technological adoption toward integrated, evidence-based approaches that demonstrably improve food safety, nutrition, accessibility, and accountability.

items.title: Smart tools for diverse minds: how AI use impacts performance and well-being among neurodivergent employees
items.abstract: Purpose This study investigates how and when AI use at work relates to neurodivergent employees’ task performance and burnout. Drawing on Sociotechnical System Theory, the study proposes that executive functioning (EF) serves as the mediating mechanism and that social support serves as the moderating factor. Design/methodology/approach The three-wave survey data were collected from 286 neurodivergent employees in the United Kingdom, enabling temporal separation of the predictor, mediator, and outcome variables to reduce concerns for common method bias. Findings Results showed that AI use at work was positively associated with EF, which in turn was positively associated with task performance and negatively associated with burnout. Social support moderated these relationships, with AI use’s benefits for EF and subsequent performance and well-being emerging only when workplace social support was high. Originality/value This study advances a sociotechnical understanding of how AI use may support neurodivergent employees. By positioning AI as external cognitive scaffolding and social support as a key social system, the study clarifies how technological and social systems work together to shape work outcomes among neurodivergent employees.

items.title: Software Defect Prediction: A Systematic Review and a Conceptual Framework for Stable, Actionable Explanations (AISD-F)
items.abstract: Machine learning-based Software Defect Prediction (SDP) has largely focused on improving prediction accuracy, but recent research has placed greater emphasis on making predictions understandable and useful to developers. This systematic review examines the use of Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) in SDP and the evidence supporting its reliability in practice. Following PRISMA guidelines, 40 peer-reviewed studies, primarily published between 2020 and 2025, were selected from IEEE Xplore, SpringerLink, ScienceDirect, Google Scholar, and Scopus. The studies were examined in terms of XAI methods, explanation reliability and stability, dataset quality, and model selection. LIME and SHAP were the most frequently used methods, yet multi-run evaluations showed changes in their feature rankings across configurations, in contrast to the reliability reported by many single-run studies. Data-quality problems, particularly SZZ-related label noise, class imbalance, and multicollinearity, often had a greater effect on prediction reliability than model architecture. The review also found growing use of line-level and just-in-time prediction, although consistent validation at industrial scale remains limited. Within the reviewed corpus, no study provides controlled evidence that XAI explanations improve developers' ability to resolve software defects, and the field currently lacks industrial-scale validation and controlled developer studies of XAI-assisted defect resolution. Based on these findings, this paper proposes the Actionable and Interpretable Software Defect Framework (AISD-F), a conceptual, five-stage modular architecture (not yet empirically validated) that is intended to integrate data quality assurance, hybrid model selection, dual-layer explanation, and CI/CD into a unified research agenda for explainable SDP, rather than a deployment-ready solution.

items.title: Software Engineering LLMs: Why We Need Them and How Software Engineering Helps Build Them
items.abstract: Software engineering (SE) expertise can shape how coding large language models (LLMs) are trained and which engineering capabilities they acquire. We examine this role through an industrial case study of capability-focused training for a 92B-parameter coding LLM serving more than 100,000 developers. We demonstrate how established SE knowledge can guide the selection of engineering capabilities, the construction of verifiable training data, and the evaluation of model improvements. To target repository-level refactoring, we developed RefactorForge, a pipeline that combines refactoring knowledge, established SE tools, and verification techniques to construct training data. Across 306 Python repositories, RefactorForge generated 5,704 executable tasks and retained 4,572 verified teacher trajectories totaling 72.51 million tokens. Incremental supervised fine-tuning on these trajectories, accounting for 0.46% of the preceding coding mixture's tokens, improved RefactorBench performance by 18.00 percentage points and SWE-Bench ProMax performance by 7.06 points. Under OpenCode, these improvements extended to SWE issue resolution, with gains of 4.97 points on SWE-Bench Verified and 1.23 points on SWE-Bench Pro. Improvements also persisted across other coding-agent harnesses, while greenfield repository generation showed mixed results. We report lessons from constructing capability-focused training data and evaluating its effects across engineering workloads. Building on this industrial experience, we propose a research agenda for expanding SE's role in transforming coding LLMs into SE LLMs: incorporating SE knowledge into model training, applying engineering methods to model development and maintenance, and systematically defining the engineering capabilities these models should acquire.

items.title: Stage-wise Extreme Atomic Proximity in HPacker Side-chain Reconstruction
items.abstract: This technical note documents stage-wise extreme atomic proximity during HPacker side-chain reconstruction of 200 stored structures from a single BioEmu wild-type protein ensemble. Six sequential reconstruction stages (0–5; 1,200 archived structures) were examined using a strict distance threshold of <1.6 Å between nonadjacent interresidue heavy atoms. At stage 5, 134 of 200 structures contained at least one such contact. For the selected PHE6–PHE55 residue pair, 43 of 200 structures exhibited an ordered contact–noncontact–contact sequence, while 25 of 200 exhibited complete six-stage alternation (10 with the pattern 010101 and 15 with 101010). Exploratory, post hoc selected local-input interventions and neural-network response diagnostics documented case-specific structural and predicted side-chain responses. In a selected WT0 example, the intervention-derived stage-5 structure increased the minimum PHE6–PHE55 heavy-atom distance from 0.2773 Å to 1.8815 Å. Four selected WT0/WT1 baseline and intervention-derived structures subsequently completed a fixed minimization and short BioEmu relaxation workflow, including 0.1 ns NVT and 0.4 ns NPT, without production molecular dynamics. A separate protein heavy-atom Lennard-Jones proxy identified severe overlap contributions in selected input geometries. The observations describe one fixed reconstruction archive and selected exploratory case studies. They do not establish a general side-chain packing improvement, a unique neural-network causal pathway, higher molecular-dynamics completion rates, or thermodynamic stabilization. items.title: StateWise: Teaching Language Models to Track and Obey Evolving Constraints in Multi-Turn Dialogue
items.abstract: Users of conversational assistants rarely state all requirements up front: they add constraints, amend them, withdraw them, digress, and return. Instruction-tuned LLMs fail here in two ways: active constraints stop being honored as turns accumulate (persistence failure), and withdrawn constraints keep being enacted (relapse). The only existing repair we know of is an external ledger that re-injects a compiled specification every turn. We propose StateWise, a self-improving approach that teaches a single LLM to maintain its own revisable constraint state, a typed state with tombstones for revoked constraints, so persistence and relapse are measured by executable checkers and ground-truth states are compiled for free. StateWise fine-tunes the LLM on two complementary skills, summarizing a dialogue into its constraint state and responding conditioned on that state, then self-trains on its own trajectories, keeping only turns that pass an exact round-trip check against the compiled state. This teaches 7-8B models to track the state almost perfectly but, surprisingly, not to obey it: on Llama-3.1-8B every supervised variant roughly doubles relapse. We therefore add a preference stage on self-generated relapse contrasts, where the rejected response enacts a revoked rule and the chosen one passes the round-trip check. On two backbones with held-out constraint families and unseen phrasings, StateWise cuts relapse by 8-22 points relative to supervised self-training, lifts conversation success by 8-19 points over the backbone, and beats an oracle compiled-ledger baseline on relapse with no inference-time scaffolding. We also characterize the recipe's cost on general instruction-following benchmarks and study weight interpolation as a mitigation.

items.title: STRATEGI GURU PENDIDIKAN PANCASILA DALAM MENINGKATKAN MORALITAS SOSIAL SISWA DI SMP NEGERI 1 TUHEMBERUA
items.abstract: ABSTRACT The decline in social morality among adolescents poses a challenge in education, as it may be reflected in a lack of discipline, low levels of responsibility, and insufficient respect for others. Through Pancasila Education, schools play a role in shaping students’ character and improving their social morality. This study aims to describe the strategies employed by Pancasila Education teachers to improve students’ social morality and to identify the supporting and inhibiting factors at SMP Negeri 1 Tuhemberua. This study employed a qualitative approach with a descriptive research design. The informants consisted of the school principal, a Pancasila Education teacher, and seventh-grade students at SMP Negeri 1 Tuhemberua, with a total of five informants. Data were collected through interviews, observations, and documentation, and analyzed through data reduction, data display, and conclusion drawing. The findings indicate that teachers’ strategies for improving students’ social morality include role modeling, the habituation of positive behaviors, the use of varied teaching methods, and positive reinforcement through appreciation of students’ behavior and achievements. The inhibiting factors include differences in students’ characteristics, the influence of family and community environments, and low intrinsic motivation among some students. Efforts to overcome these challenges include character development through religious activities, linking learning materials to real-life moral issues, and fostering collaboration among schools, parents, and the community. This study emphasizes that improving students’ social morality requires the consistent implementation of character education strategies and sustained support from their surrounding environments. ABSTRAK Penurunan moralitas sosial di kalangan remaja menjadi tantangan dalam dunia pendidikan karena dapat tercermin melalui perilaku kurang disiplin, rendahnya tanggung jawab, dan kurangnya sikap saling menghargai. Sekolah melalui pembelajaran Pendidikan Pancasila memiliki peran dalam membentuk karakter dan meningkatkan moralitas sosial siswa. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk mendeskripsikan strategi guru Pendidikan Pancasila dalam meningkatkan moralitas sosial siswa serta mengidentifikasi faktor pendukung dan penghambatnya di SMP Negeri 1 Tuhemberua. Penelitian ini menggunakan pendekatan kualitatif dengan jenis deskriptif. Informan penelitian terdiri atas kepala sekolah, guru PPKn, dan siswa kelas VII SMP Negeri 1 Tuhemberua, dengan jumlah keseluruhan 5 orang. Data dikumpulkan melalui wawancara, observasi, dan dokumentasi, kemudian dianalisis melalui reduksi data, penyajian data, dan penarikan kesimpulan. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa strategi guru dalam meningkatkan moralitas sosial siswa dilakukan melalui keteladanan, pembiasaan perilaku positif, penggunaan metode pembelajaran yang bervariasi, serta pemberian penguatan positif berupa apresiasi terhadap perilaku dan pencapaian siswa. Faktor penghambat meliputi perbedaan karakter siswa, pengaruh lingkungan keluarga dan masyarakat, serta rendahnya motivasi internal sebagian siswa. Upaya mengatasi kendala tersebut dilakukan melalui pembinaan karakter dalam kegiatan keagamaan, pengaitan materi pembelajaran dengan kasus moral dalam kehidupan sehari-hari, serta kerja sama antara sekolah, orang tua, dan masyarakat. Penelitian ini menegaskan bahwa peningkatan moralitas sosial siswa memerlukan penerapan strategi pendidikan karakter secara konsisten dan dukungan lingkungan yang berkesinambungan.

items.title: STRATEGI MAHASISWA DALAM PENYUSUNAN KARYA TULIS ILMIAH: STUDI LITERATUR
items.abstract: Writing scientific papers is an academic competence that every student is expected to master, yet many students still find it difficult to complete well. This article aims to examine the obstacles students face and the strategies they use in writing scientific papers, as well as the wise use of artificial intelligence. The method used is a literature review of eight Indonesian journal articles published between 2021 and 2025. The data were analyzed descriptively and qualitatively through data reduction, grouping of information, interpretation, and drawing conclusions. The findings indicate that students’ obstacles include difficulty in developing ideas, limited and poorly managed sources, errors in citation and paraphrasing, language mechanics, low self-efficacy and motivation, and unstable mood. The strategies reported in the literature include choosing an interesting topic, reading extensively, adjusting to the target journal’s format, joining writing training and coaching clinics, analyzing mentor texts, using reference managers, seeking feedback from supervisors and peers, building self-efficacy and academic motivation, and using artificial intelligence responsibly. Students therefore need to combine technical, social, psychological, and technological strategies, supported by their institutions.

items.title: Symbolic Persona Coding as a Semantic Encoding Protocol for LLM-Based Code Generation
items.abstract: Abstract Large language models (LLMs) receive behavioral requirements through multiple representational formats, including natural-language instructions, symbolic conventions, and structured data. Although these formats differ in explicitness, semantic organization, and reuse cost, their comparative effects on code-generation performance require systematic evaluation. This paper presents a methodological framework for investigating Symbolic Persona Coding (SPC) as a semantic encoding protocol for LLM-based code generation. The framework specifies seven instruction conditions spanning long and short natural-language prompts, SPC symbols with inline definitions, semantically matched plain-language labels, reusable system-level definitions, structured JSON specifications, and an undefined-symbol control. It defines an evaluation procedure combining hidden functional tests, static compliance checks, token accounting, response-latency measurement, and repeated-run analysis. Particular attention is given to distinguishing the effects of symbolic notation from those of instruction content, prompt length, and reusable definitions. Publicly available, provider-specific experimental harnesses are provided as implementation references to support independent investigation. The framework is methodological rather than empirical: no comparative performance results are claimed. Its contribution is a structured and reproducible basis for evaluating instruction representations under explicitly defined experimental conditions. The study is limited to code generation and does not assess the broader SPC framework's applications to affective and abstract meaning, human-AI relationship formation, or interaction dynamics. Keywords: Symbolic Persona Coding; large language models; code generation; semantic encoding; instruction compliance; experimental methodology; reproducibility Disclaimer This paper presents a proposed experimental methodology and a preliminary implementation reference. The author has not conducted the model evaluations described in the protocol and makes no empirical claim that SPC improves functional correctness, instruction compliance, token efficiency, latency, or performance stability. The proposed conditions, evaluation measures, and implementation require independent verification before use in confirmatory research. Any findings obtained through subsequent implementation should be interpreted within the tested task set, model configurations, execution environment, and measurement procedures. The code-generation focus is a deliberate methodological restriction and does not constitute a comprehensive evaluation or definition of SPC, whose broader scope includes affective and abstract meaning, interaction patterns, and human-AI relationship formation. Author's Note This paper was developed to make a specific component of Symbolic Persona Coding available for systematic investigation. SPC is not intended solely as a prompt-compression technique or as an alternative notation for conventional instructions. Its broader design focuses on affective and abstract meaning, interactional patterns, and the formation of relationships between humans and language models. It uses compact symbolic representations and codes to establish recognizable semantic structures that can guide a model toward expanding the meanings associated with those structures within an interaction. The examples and experimental conditions presented in this paper represent a limited application of that broader design. They focus on code generation because this domain permits the specification of functional tests, explicit behavioral constraints, and measurable resource costs. The resulting evaluation framework should not be interpreted as a complete representation of SPC, nor should its scope be used to infer conclusions about SPC's broader affective and relational applications. Those applications require distinct research questions, operational definitions, and evaluation methods. The distinction between design intent and demonstrated performance is equally important. This paper proposes a way to investigate whether a particular form of symbolic encoding produces measurable effects under controlled conditions. It does not claim that the intended effects have already been established, that symbolic codes are universally interpretable by LLMs, or that compact representations necessarily improve performance. The model's interpretation of a symbol, the consistency of that interpretation across contexts, and the practical value of the resulting behavior are empirical questions rather than assumptions built into the framework. The work is also intended as an invitation to independent examination. Researchers may question the selection of conditions, the adequacy of semantic equivalence, the validity of the evaluation measures, or the generalizability of future results. These are substantive methodological questions that should be addressed through transparent implementation, controlled comparison, and replication. The public harnesses are provided as starting points for that process, not as substitutes for independent verification. The purpose of this paper is consequently narrow but deliberate: to translate one operational aspect of SPC into a form that can be examined, challenged, and refined through empirical research. Its claims should be judged within that scope, while the broader framework remains open to investigation through methods suited to its affective, abstract, and relational dimensions.
